<thought>The proton NMR spectra show signals at 7.47 ppm and 7.64 ppm, which are typical for aromatic protons. The splitting patterns (dddd and tt) suggest a complex aromatic system, possibly a substituted benzene ring. Given the carbon NMR data and the proton NMR data, the compound likely contains an aromatic ring with a carbonyl group. To further narrow down the structure, I will check the IR spectra for functional group information, particularly to confirm the presence of a carbonyl group.</thought>
<action>ir_spectra</action>
<action_input>{}</action_input>

<thought>The IR spectra show a strong absorption at 1737 cm⁻¹, which is characteristic of a carbonyl group, likely an ester or ketone. The presence of peaks around 3100 cm⁻¹ suggests aromatic C-H stretching, supporting the presence of an aromatic ring. The peaks at 3550 and 3475 cm⁻¹ could indicate O-H stretching, possibly from an alcohol or phenol group. Given the data, the compound likely contains an aromatic ring with a carbonyl group and possibly an alcohol or phenol group. To further refine the structure, I will use the mass spectrometry spectra to determine the molecular weight and possible fragments.</thought>
<action>mass_spectrometry_spectra</action>
<action_input>{}</action_input>

<thought>The mass spectrometry data shows a major peak at m/z 121.05, which is likely the molecular ion peak, indicating a molecular weight of approximately 121 g/mol. This mass is consistent with a benzene ring (78 g/mol) plus additional functional groups. Given the presence of a carbonyl group and possibly an alcohol or phenol group, a likely candidate is a compound like salicylaldehyde (C7H6O2), which has a molecular weight of 122 g/mol. The slight discrepancy could be due to isotopic variations or fragmentation patterns. To confirm, I will search for isomers of C7H6O2 and validate the SMILES string for salicylaldehyde.</thought>
